THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.12.2024, ALONG WITH MACA.1609/2017, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 1609 & 2279 OF 2017 4  2024:KER:94902  JUDGMENT Dated this the 10th day of December, 2024
The petitioner in O.P.MV No.119/2014 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Muvattupuzha is the appellant in M.A.C.A.No.1609/2017.
The 3rd respondent in the original petition is the appellant in M.A.C.A.No.2279/2017.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereinafter referred to as arrayed in the original petition before the Tribunal.

The petitioner filed the above original petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation on account of the injuries sustained by her in an accident that occurred on 11.07.2013.
2. According to the petitioner, On 11.07.2013 at 9.30 a.m., she was going to the college on her Scooter bearing Reg.No.44/A 9460.

When the scooter reached the place called Karukadam, an autorikshaw bearing Reg.No.KL-17/B 9539 driven by the 2 nd respondent hit on the scooter of the petitioner and as a result of which she sustained serious injuries.
She had lost her eye sight of both eyes.
She had sustained fracture of the hip, acetabulam etc.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2 nd 2024:KER:94902 respondent, who was driving the offending vehicle.
The 1 st respondent is the owner and the 3rd respondent is the insurer.
She claimed a total compensation of Rs.2,25,03000/-, which was limited to 2 Crores.
Though notice was served on the respondents 1 and 2, they remained exparte.
The 3rd respondent entered appearance and filed written statement admitting the accident, but, contending that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Therefore, the 3 rd respondent denied the liability to pay compensation to the petitioner.
From the side of the petitioner, PW1 was examined.
Exts. A1
to A37
were marked.
Ext.X1 was also marked.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
3. After hearing the parties and evaluating the evidence, the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.98,32,620/-.
4. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred M.A.C.A.No.1609/2017 and the 3rd respondent preferred M.A.C.A.No.2279/2017.
5. Now the point that arise for consideration is, whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just 2024:KER:94902 and reasonable.

sentences.text:
Heard Smt.Aney Paul, learned Counsel for the petitioner, Sri.Latheesh Sebastian, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent in M.A.C.A No.1609/2017 and Sri.K.S.Santhi,
learned Counsel appearing for the appellant insurance company in M.A.C.A.No.2279 of 2017.
7. The fact that the petitioner, at the time of accident, was working in Ilahia College of Engineering and Technology, Mulavoor is not disputed.

entities.text: Ilahia College of Engineering and Technology, Mulavoor
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: She was aged 32 years.

The case of the petitioner is that she had a monthly salary of Rs.32,000/- It was argued by the learned Counsel for the 3rd respondent that the documents produced by the petitioner does not reveal that she was drawing a salary of Rs.32,000/- per month.
However, on a perusal of Ext.A37, it can be seen that she received different amounts as salary during different months including some amounts above Rs.30,000/- per month.
Therefore, I find no merit in the argument that the monthly income of the petitioner was less than Rs.30,000/-.

In other words, I find that the monthly income of the petitioner fixed at Rs.30,000/- is just and reasonable.
2024
On the basis of Ext.X1 disability certificate, the disability of the petitioner was assessed as 90% by the Tribunal.
The petitioner was working as Assistant Professor and in the accident she lost eye sight of both eyes.
She sustained the following injuries as noted in Ext.A7 wound certificate.
The injuries noted are: Lacerated wound on the right cheek, crush injury with depressed fracture of forehead, bleeding from the nose, lacerated wound on the tongue.
Lacerated wound on the right arm and right leg, pain and tenderness of hip and right thigh.
C.T.scan showed multiple fracture of both maxilla.
Ext .A9 case summary shows that the petitioner was admitted on 11.07.2013 with extensive facial and ophthalmic injuries.
Ext.A10 is the C.T.scan report of brain and face.

It show that the petitioner had sustained fracture of roof, floor, medial and lateral walls of bilateral orbits with pneumo orbit and hyperdense foci noted on the left side, fracture medial wall of left optic canal,
fracture of bilateral nasal bones, fractures of bilateral maxillary, ethmoidal, frontal and left sphenoid sinus with hemosinus, fracture of bilateral zygomatic arch, fracture of bilateral frontal bone, fracture of bilateral maxilla.
Ext.A12 is the Ophthalmologist report which shows that the petitioner had sustained penetrating injury with corneosclear tear.
Ext .A13 discharge summary show that she was admitted on 11.07.2013 and discharged on 29.07.2013 with right eye penetrating injury, left eye globe rupture.
Ext.A14 shows that she was admitted on 1.8.2013 and discharged on 6.8.2013.
Ext .A16 is M.R.I copy of right knee.
Ext .A17 discharge summary shows that she was admitted on 29.09.2013 and discharged on 4.10.2013.
Ext.A19 shows that she was again admitted on 3.12.2013 and discharged on 17.12.2013.
Ext.A20 discharge summary shows that she was again admitted on 6.2.2014 and discharged on 6.3.2014.
Ext.A21 discharge summary issued from Sreedhareeyam Ayurveda Eye hospital which shows that she was 2024:KER:94902 admitted there from 12.1.2015 to 8.2.2015.
Ext.A22 is the medical report from Comtrust Eye hospital, Calicut which show that she had loss of vision in both eyes.
On examination of right eye vision was minimal perception of light with inaccurate PR.

sentences.text: From Ext.A29 certificate, it can be seen that the petitioner was M-Tech Degree holder with first rank, from Anna University, Coimbatore.
From the evidence it is revealed that the petitioner lost eye sight of both eyes, due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Since she became blind, she was terminated from service, as per Ext.A36 termination letter issued by the Ilahia College of Engineering and Technology, Muvattupuzha.

entities.text: Ilahia College of Engineering and Technology, Muvattupuzha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned Counsel for the petitioner would argue that the petitioner was incapacitated from doing the job of Assistant Professor or any other job, any more.

Therefore, according to him, the functional disability of the petitioner is to be fixed at 100%.
10.

In the decision in Rajendran M. v. Union of India, 2017 (5) KHC 222, while considering what amounts to 100% disability, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph 46 to 49 held that :-
46.

entities.text: Rajendran M. v. Union of India, 2017 (5) KHC 222
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Existence is not animalistic.
Nor is human existence mere survival.
It is more than that.
The survival instinct being an evolutionary essence, man tries under all circumstances to preserve himself--to survive as a necessity and to thrive as a possibility, even as a desirability.
So, man's survival mechanism never permits him to be sedentary.
He works.
Work is man, or at least man is what he does.

We glorify 2024:KER:94902 ourselves by what we do;
our profession is our identity, our essence, and our very being.
(One gender is expressed to avoid the infelicity of employing the dual gender--man and woman--for which English has no personal pronoun.

Woman always equates Man--and perhaps more.)
47.
So, a surgeon, after losing his hand in an accident, can still be, say, a guard at the very hospital.
He can still earn.
Then can we say he has not lost capacity to do any work?

Dignity of labour apart,
and the survival instinct not discounted, an Einstein having lost his ability, by an accident or otherwise, is no longer an Einstein; he is just one in the multitude, an insignificant spec merely existing.
So "all capacity to do any work" should be understood to mean all capacity to do any work of his calling for which he or she has skill and training.
Nothing else.
48. An accident victim, a driver, lost his right leg - had it amputated.
His physical disability was estimated at 40%.
But the question is whether it would amount to 100% disability professionally.

The Supreme Court in S.Suresh v. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd and another15 has relied on Pratap Narain Singh Deo v. Srinivas Sabata, 1976 KHC 610 : 1976 (1) SCC 289 : 1976 SCC (L&S) 52 : AIR 1976 SC 222, and held that it would amount to total disablement in terms of S.2(1)(1) of the Workmen's Compensation Act, if such disablement, whether temporary or permanent, incapacitates workman for all work which he could perform at the time of the accident.
49.

entities.text: Pratap Narain Singh Deo v. Srinivas Sabata, 1976 KHC 610 : 1976 (1) SCC 289 : 1976 SCC (L&S) 52 : AIR 1976 SC 222
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Be it a carpenter or a driver, S.Suresh went on to observe, sustained an injury of such a nature as to permanently disable him, the question would be "whether the disablement incapacitated the respondent for all work which he was capable of performing at the time of the accident."
It answered in the affirmative."

5 11.

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance ... vs Sumitha Madhavan Kartha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the decision in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar and 2024:KER:94902 Another, (2011) 1 SCC 343,
with regard to the manner of ascertaining the effect of permanent disability on the actual earning capacity, in paragraph 10, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows :
"Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar and 2024:KER:94902 Another, (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.

If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.
...."
12. In the decision in Jakir Hussein v. Sabir and Others, (2015) 7 SCC 252, the insured was a driver whose right hand was completely crushed and deformed in an accident.

entities.text: Jakir Hussein v. Sabir and Others, (2015) 7 SCC 252
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor has assessed his permanent disability at 55%.

In the above context, the Hon'ble Apex Court held in paragraph 15 as follows :
2024:KER:94902 "..........

However, it is important to consider the relevant fact namely that the appellant is a driver and driving the motor vehicle is the only means of livelihood for himself as well as the members of his family.
Further, it is very crucial to note that the High Court has clearly observed that his right hand was completely crushed and deformed.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (supra),
this Court specifically gave the illustration of a driver who has permanent disablement of hand and stated that the loss of future earnings capacity would be virtually 100%.
Therefore, clearly when it comes to loss of earning due to permanent disability, the same may be treated as 100% loss caused to the appellant since he will never be able to work as a driver again.

"
13. Since the petitioner lost eye sight of both eyes due to the injuries sustained in the accident, and she was terminated from service because of the blindness, though as per Ext.X1 certificate, her disability was assessed as 90%, I hold that her functional disability is to be fixed as 100%.
Icici Lombard General Insurance ... vs Sumitha Madhavan Kartha on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120037722/
6 14.

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance ... vs Sumitha Madhavan Kartha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the monthly income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.30,000/-, her annual income will come to Rs.3,60,000/-.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that during the year 2013 - 14, the petitioner was liable to pay income tax for the income exceeding Rs.2,00,000/-, at the rate of 10% upto Rs.5,00,000/- and hence, the income tax payable by her is to be deducted from her annual income.
The learned counsel for the petitioner also fairly 2024:KER:94902 conceded to the above submission made by the learned counsel for the respondent.

As per the decision in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121 also, where the annual income is in the taxable rate, the word "actual salary" should be read as "actual salary less tax".

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The income tax payable by the petitioner during the year 2013 - 14, for annual income of Rs.360,000/- will come to Rs.16,000/-.
Therefore, the annual income of the petitioner less the income tax payable thereto during the year 2013 - 14, will come to Rs.3,44,000/- (3,60,000 -16000).

As she was aged 32 at the time of accident, 40% of the above income is to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier to be applied is 16, in the light of the decision in National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC).

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore the loss of earning power on account of the disability will come to Rs.77,05,600/-(3,44,000+40% of 344,600 x 16).(481,600x16)
15.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that since the disability is taken as 100%,
further compensation under the head 'loss of earnings' is not required.

However, it is revealed that because of the injuries sustained in the 2024:KER:94902 accident, the appellant could not go for work for nearly seven months, during the period prior to the date of filing of the original petition.

Therefore, I hold that towards loss of earning she is entitled for an amount of Rs.2,10,000/-, for the above seven months (Rs.30,000/- x 7)
16.
Though an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- was claimed by the petitioner towards the head extra nourishment, no amount was granted by the Tribunal.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I hold that Rs.1,00,000/- can be granted towards the afore head.

17. The learned Standing Counsel for the 3 rd respondent submits that, an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-
was granted by the Tribunal under the head future bystander expenses, which is on the higher side.

Considering the fact that she lost her eye sight of both eyes and is incapacitated from pursuing her job because of the injuries sustained in the accident, I hold that the amount awarded by the Tribunal under the head bystander expenses is just and reasonable.
18. The Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards future medical expenses.
The learned Counsel for the 2024:KER:94902 petitioner produced medical bills for an amount Rs.34,690/- for the period after passing the award.
It shows that he needs further treatment and therefore, further expenditure on that head is still required.
However, Rs.2,00,000/- awarded on this head is on the higher side.
Considering the above facts, I am inclined to reduce the compensation on that head to Rs.1,50,000/-.

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance ... vs Sumitha Madhavan Kartha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal granted Rs.15,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and convenience in life and another Rs.10,00,000/- towards disfigurement, which according to the 3rd respondent is on the higher side.
The petitioner appeared before the Tribunal and the Tribunal found that 'she was a very beautiful lady and after the accident there is depression on the head.
It is true that she had lost eye sight of both eyes.
It is also true that her face is deformed.
But she was able to answer the questions properly.

20. Considering the fact that the petitioner was aged only 32 years at the time of accident and she has to continue with her disfigurement through out her life, I hold that the amount granted under the head disfigurement is just and reasonable.
However, I am of the view that the amount awarded under the head loss of amenities 2024:KER:94902 and convenience in life is on the higher side.

Hence, I reduce it to Rs.10,00,000/-.
21.

Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads, as it appears to be just and reasonable.

22. Accordingly the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant/claimant is awarded compensation of Rs.1,21,12,620/- with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation with proportionate costs.

The 3rd respondent in the original petition is the appellant in M.A.C.A.No.2279/2017.
The petitioner filed the above original petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation on account of the injuries sustained by her in an accident that occurred on 11.07.2013.
She had lost her eye sight of both eyes.
She had sustained fracture of the hip, acetabulam etc.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2 nd 2024:KER:94902 respondent, who was driving the offending vehicle.
She claimed a total compensation of Rs.2,25,03000/-, which was limited to 2 Crores.
Though notice was served on the respondents 1 and 2, they remained exparte.
Therefore, the 3 rd respondent denied the liability to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. After hearing the parties and evaluating the evidence, the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.98,32,620/-.
4. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred M.A.C.A.No.1609/2017 and the 3rd respondent preferred M.A.C.A.No.2279/2017.
From the evidence it is revealed that the petitioner lost eye sight of both eyes, due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Since she became blind, she was terminated from service, as per Ext.A36 termination letter issued by the Ilahia College of Engineering and Technology, Muvattupuzha.
